feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 4 (12 mm footprints, ±0.08 m span, y=0.03 m) gave zero oval and slalom line losses, but the s-bend still lost the line once per run (max_error 0.0645 m), and the score was 53.53. Iteration 2 showed that moving the row forward to y=0.05 m raised oval max_error from 0.0613 to 0.0637 m and brought back slalom line losses, so forward is rejected. Iteration 3 (16 mm, same span and row) also lost the s-bend line once, so the footprint is not the s-bend lever on its own. In the controller I hold kp 8.0, ki 0.05, kd 0.3 and the weights fixed, because nothing in the evidence yet isolates a controller change. Decide the next step from the race: if line_loss_events falls to zero on the s-bend and oval max_error stays near 0.061 m, hold the geometry and the controller. If the s-bend still loses the line at y=0.01 m, the row position is not the limit, so hold the geometry and treat controller bias as the remaining cause. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2, reduce mass to 0.5 kg.
requested_changes: If the s-bend still shows line_loss_events of 1 or more at y=0.01 m, hold sensor positions, sensor_size 0.012 and mass 0.6 kg, because the row has then been tested at both 0.03 and 0.01 m with the loss still present; the limit is controller bias, not geometry.
If line losses are zero but oval max_error rises above 0.0629 m at y=0.01 m, return the row to y=0.02 m as a midpoint, since y=0.03 m gave 0.0629 m and y=0.05 m gave 0.0637 m.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 with the rearward row, reduce mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg with sensor positions unchanged, since iteration 4 showed 0.168 on the oval and 0.158 on the s-bend.
